title: Who played on the Black Patti record and trying to find a copy
summary: They discuss who was on the Black Patti record, whose copies survive, and where the company was.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well, that Boer Hog Blues and the Squeeze Me, do you remember just who was on that? Was that the same group you told about with John Lindsay? Yeah.
That was on the Boer Hog.
Yeah. That was, well that wasn't the same group that made the number, because she was with, yeah.
Oh, your wife played on that record too?

Yeah, no, not on the record. We played, that was the same band that played the number, but she didn't play on the record. No, Mine played on the record. He played on the record. Yeah, that's the, that's the, it squeezed me. It squeezed me in that one. And since I've lost all my stuff, see when I come out of 4914 Forestville, I was practically stranded, and all that stuff was lost in storage, and I've been trying to get a record, and I haven't been able to get that Black Patty yet, and I've sent all the way to New York. I lost all that stuff in storage. Oh, for sure. Now, I think Baby Dots has got one. There's two or three of the musicians that's got them around here, and they wouldn't let me get my hands on them. They wouldn't let me even see them.
If Baby's got it, he wouldn't let me see it. I don't know that I, I don't believe Baby has one. I've never seen it over there.

No? Well, why did you get it at that? First, I found an old cracked copy years ago. I had a crack all the way up to the center. Yeah. And I gave that away. It would hardly play. I straight had to break my needle. Yeah.
I gave it to some kid from California.

One begged me for it, and I gave it to him. Uh-huh. And then I found another one in Chicago a few years ago, and mine is pretty worn. Sometime maybe I can make a copy of it for you. Yeah. I'll try it.
Well, this company went out of business.
This company was on Madison Street. They were on Madison. Yeah, they were on Madison.
Yeah, they were on Madison. Yeah, they were on Madison. I think around 10 hundred, somewheres out there. That's where you made the record. That's where we made the record. Yeah.
And someday I'll try to get a copy of that for you.
